name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project with customized Dockerfile and .dockerfile files.

Containerize the ASP.NET (.NET Framework), not .NET Core, project in the settings below, focusing **exclusively** on changes required to run it in a Windows Docker container. Use specified settings; unspecified settings use defaults.

Settings: project `.csproj` path; Windows Server SKU (Core default or Full) and version (2016/2019/2022); custom build/run base images (default None); primary/additional exposed ports; container user (default `ContainerUser`); IIS settings; pre/post build steps; GAC assemblies and versions; MSIs and versions; COM components; registry paths/values; environment variables (default Use defaults); Windows roles/features; files/directories relative to project root and container destinations; exclusions; additional `.dockerignore` patterns; health-check URL, interval and timeout; other requirements; known issues.

✅ App configuration modification to ensure config builders are used to read app settings and connection strings from the environment variables  
✅ Dockerfile creation and configuration for an ASP.NET application  
✅ Specifying multiple stages in the Dockerfile to build/publish the application and copy the output to the final image  
✅ Configuration of Windows container platform compatibility (Windows Server Core or Full)  
✅ Proper handling of dependencies (GAC assemblies, MSIs, COM components)  
❌ No infrastructure setup (assumed to be handled separately)  
❌ No code changes beyond those required for containerization

1. Review settings.
2. Create `progress.md` to track changes with check marks.
3. Determine .NET Framework version from `.csproj` `TargetFrameworkVersion`.
4. Select Windows Server image based on framework version, SKU, and version. Tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
5. Ensure required NuGet packages are installed. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If they are not installed, the user must install them manually. If they are not installed, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console. The following packages are required:
`Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`
6. Modify `web.config`: add ConfigBuilders section in `configSections`; add `configBuilders` section in root; configure EnvironmentConfigBuilder for `appSettings` and `connectionStrings`:
`<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />`
`<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />`
Use `<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">` and `<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">`, retaining existing settings.
7. Create `LogMonitorConfig.json` in the Dockerfile folder by copying the reference below. The file's contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless instructions in containerization settings specify otherwise. In particular, make sure the level of issues to be logged is not changed as using `Information` level for EventLog sources will cause unnecessary noise.
8. Create a root `Dockerfile` with multiple stages. Build: Windows Server Core; use `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk` unless a custom build image is specified; copy sln, csproj, and `packages.config` first; copy `NuGet.config` if present and configure private feeds; restore NuGet packages; copy remaining source and build/publish to `C:\publish` using MSBuild. Final: selected Windows Server image; use `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/aspnet` unless a custom run image is specified; copy `LogMonitorConfig.json` to a container directory (e.g. `C:\LogMonitor`); download LogMonitor.exe from https://github.com/microsoft/windows-container-tools/releases/download/v2.1.1/LogMonitor.exe to that directory; set working directory `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`; copy `C:\publish` output; configure entry point to run LogMonitor.exe with ServiceMonitor.exe to monitor IIS:
`ENTRYPOINT [ "C:\\LogMonitor\\LogMonitor.exe", "C:\\ServiceMonitor.exe", "w3svc" ]`
Account for SKU/version, user, GAC, COM, roles/features, and file copying. Customize the example to project settings. **IMPORTANT:** Use a Windows Server Core base image unless the user has **specifically requested** a full Windows Server image in the settings file
9. Create root `.dockerignore`. The `.dockerignore` file **MUST** include at least the following elements as well as additional patterns as specified in the containerization settings: any additional patterns specified in settings.
10. Add Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` if a health-check endpoint is provided.
11. Add to project file: `<None Include="Dockerfile" />`
12. Mark tasks complete: `[ ]` → `[✓]`
13. Continue until all tasks are complete and Docker build succeeds. Confirm success using:
`docker build -t aspnet-app:latest .`
If build fails, review errors and adjust Dockerfile or project configuration. Report success/failure.

Maintain `progress.md` with this structure:
[ ] .NET Framework version detection (version: ___)
[ ] Windows Server SKU selection (SKU: ___)
[ ] Windows Server version selection (Version: ___)
[ ] Web.config modifications for configuration builders
[ ] NuGet package source configuration (if applicable)
[ ] Copy LogMonitorConfig.json and adjust if required by settings
[ ] .dockerignore file creation
[ ] Build stage created with SDK image
[ ] sln, csproj, packages.config, and (if applicable) NuGet.config copied for package restore
[ ] Runtime stage created with runtime image
[ ] Non-root user configuration
[ ] Dependency handling (GAC, MSI, COM, registry, additional files, etc.)
[ ] Health check configuration (if applicable)
[ ] Special requirements implementation
[ ] Review containerization settings and make sure that all requirements are met
[ ] Docker build success
